```{r cars}
# Import data sets
car_theft_map<- "/Volumes/Editing/Bellevue Univ/Masters in Data Science/DSC 640 Data Presentation and Visualization/Week 5 & 6/Datasets/carTheftsMap.csv"
kia_thefts  <- "/Volumes/Editing/Bellevue Univ/Masters in Data Science/DSC 640 Data Presentation and Visualization/Week 5 & 6/Datasets/kiaHyundaiThefts.csv"
milwaukee_data  <- "/Volumes/Editing/Bellevue Univ/Masters in Data Science/DSC 640 Data Presentation and Visualization/Week 5 & 6/Datasets/KiaHyundaiMilwaukeeData.csv"
motherboard_data <- "/Volumes/Editing/Bellevue Univ/Masters in Data Science/DSC 640 Data Presentation and Visualization/Week 5 & 6/Datasets/Motherboard VICE News Kia Hyundai Theft Data.xlsx"

# Read in the files into a dataframe
car_theft_map <- read.csv(file =car_theft_map, header= TRUE)
kia_thefts <- read.csv(file =kia_thefts, header= TRUE)
milwaukee_data <- read.csv(file =milwaukee_data , header= TRUE)
motherboard_data <- read_excel(motherboard_data, skip = 2)
```

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
car_theft_map <- car_theft_map %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("countCarThefts"), as.numeric))
# Create date column for time series
kia_thefts <- kia_thefts %>%
  mutate(date = ymd(paste(year, month, "01")))

milwaukee_data <- milwaukee_data %>%
  mutate(date = ymd(paste(year, month, "01")))

```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
```{r}
# Filter results to the most recent year 
national_2022 <- kia_thefts %>%
    filter(year== 2022)
```


```{r}
# Distribution of Kia/Hyundai thefts in 2022
hist(national_2022$countKiaHyundaiThefts,main="Theft Histogram",xlab="Kia Hyundai Thefts")
```
```{r}
national_2022 <- kia_thefts %>%
  filter(year == 2022) %>%
summarise(
    KiaHyundai = sum(countKiaHyundaiThefts, na.rm = TRUE),
    Other = sum(countOtherThefts, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Type", values_to = "Count") %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = Count / sum(Count) * 100,
    Label = paste0(Type, "\n", comma(Count), " thefts\n(", 
                   round(Percentage, 1), "%)")
  )
# Create the pie chart using geom_bar
pie_chart <- ggplot(national_2022, aes(x = "", y = Count, fill = Type)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1, color = "white") +
  coord_polar("y", start = 0) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("KiaHyundai" = "red", "Other" = "grey")) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Label), 
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            size = 5, fontface = "bold", color = "white") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 18, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12, color = "gray30")
  ) +
    # Create labels for the chart
  labs(
    title = "Kia & Hyundai: A Disproportionate Share of Vehicle Thefts",
    subtitle = "National Data - 2022"
  )

# ggsave("01_pie_chart_national.png", pie_chart, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)

pie_chart

```

```{r}
# Find peak month for Milwaukee
milwaukee_peak <- milwaukee_data %>%
  arrange(desc(countKiaHyundaiThefts)) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  select(countKiaHyundaiThefts, countOtherThefts, month, year) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(countKiaHyundaiThefts, countOtherThefts),
               names_to = "Type", values_to = "Count") %>%
  mutate(
    Type = ifelse(Type == "countKiaHyundaiThefts", "Kia/Hyundai", "Other Vehicles"),
    Percentage = Count / sum(Count) * 100,
    ymax = cumsum(Percentage),
    ymin = c(0, head(ymax, n = -1)),
    labelPosition = (ymax + ymin) / 2,
    label = paste0(round(Percentage, 1), "%")
  )

```


```{r}
donut_chart <- ggplot(milwaukee_peak, aes(ymax = ymax, ymin = ymin, 
                                          xmax = 4, xmin = 3, fill = Type)) +
  geom_rect(color = "white", size = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Kia/Hyundai" = "#C62828", "Other Vehicles" = "#BDBDBD")) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  xlim(c(2, 4)) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 18, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11, color = "gray30")
  ) +
  geom_text(aes(x = 3.5, y = labelPosition, label = label), 
            size = 6, fontface = "bold") +
  labs(
    title = "Milwaukee's Theft Crisis at Its Peak",
    subtitle = paste0(milwaukee_peak$month[1], " ", milwaukee_peak$year[1], 
                     " - Over 3 in 4 stolen vehicles were Kia or Hyundai")
  )
```

```{r}
top_cities <- kia_thefts %>%
  filter(year == 2022) %>%
  group_by(city, state) %>%
  summarise(
    KiaHyundai = sum(countKiaHyundaiThefts, na.rm = TRUE),
    Other = sum(countOtherThefts, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Total = KiaHyundai + Other,
         Location = paste0(city, ", ", state)) %>%
  arrange(desc(KiaHyundai)) %>%
  head(10) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(KiaHyundai, Other), 
               names_to = "Type", values_to = "Count") %>%
  mutate(
    Type = ifelse(Type == "KiaHyundai", "Kia/Hyundai", "Other Vehicles"),
    Location = factor(Location, levels = unique(Location))
  )
```


```{r}

stacked_bar <- ggplot(top_cities, aes(x = reorder(Location, -Count), y = Count, fill = Type)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Kia/Hyundai" = "red", "Other Vehicles" = "grey")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Cities Hit Hardest by the Kia/Hyundai Theft Wave",
    subtitle = "Top 10 Cities by Kia/Hyundai Theft Volume - 2022",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of Vehicle Thefts"
  )
```

```{r}
# motherboard_data data set 
# Clean column names
df_raw <- clean_names(motherboard_data)

# Inspect column names to identify pattern
colnames(df_raw)

# Add a vector of the city names
cities <- c(
  "Denver", "El_Paso", "Portland", "Atlanta", "Chicago", "Virginia_Beach",
  "Louisville", "San_Diego", "Sacramento", "Dallas", "Fort_Worth",
  "Bakersfield", "Omaha_NE", "Lubbock_TX", "Fremont_CA",
  "San_Antonio", "Irving_Texas", "Madison_WI", "Frisco_TX", "Lincoln_NE", "Wichita_KS",
  "Plano_TX", "Akron_OH", "Buffalo_NY", "Chula_Vista_CA", "Reno_NV","Oxnard_CA"
  ,"San_Francisco","McKinney_TX","Arlington_TX","Garland_TX","Riverside County_CA"
  ,"Stockton_CA","Corpus_Cristi_TX","Cincinatti","Montgomery_County_MD","Henderson_NV"
  ,"San_Bernardino_CA","Newport_News_VA","Amarillo_TX","New Haven_CT","Washington_D.C."
  ,"Boise_ID","Austin, TX", "Chandler, AZ","Modesto_CA","San_Jose_CA","Aurora_IL"
  ,"Vancouver_WA","Raleigh_NC","St.Petersburg_FL","Milwaukee_WI","Los_Angeles_CA"
  ,"Glendale_AZ","Orlando_FL","Eugene_OR","Rochester_NY","Durham_NC","Norfolk_VA"
  ,"Pittsburgh_PA","Miami_FL","Spokane_WA","Salt_Lake_City_UT","Minneapolis_MN"
  ,"Anaheim_CA","Providence_RI","Syracuse_NY","Peoria_AZ","Houston_TX"
  ,"Prince_Georges_County_MD"
)

# Generate dynamic column names for all cities
new_names <- c("month", unlist(lapply(cities, function(c) {
    paste0(c, c("_kia_hyundais", "_all", "_percent"))
})))

# Apply to data frame 
colnames(df_raw)[1:length(new_names)] <- new_names

# Convert all columns except month to numeric
df_raw <- df_raw %>%
  mutate(across(-month, ~as.numeric(as.character(.x))))

#Pivot longer to combine all cities into one tidy table
df_long <- df_raw %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -month,
    names_to = c("city", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "(.*)_(kia_hyundais|all|percent)"
  )
```


```{r}
# Create treemap of average Kia/Hyundai theft rate by city
df_long%>%
  group_by(city) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_kia_hyundais = mean(kia_hyundais, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_all = mean(all, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_percent = mean(percent, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_kia_hyundais)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 15) %>%
  mutate(Label = paste0(city, "\n", comma(avg_kia_hyundais))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(area = avg_kia_hyundais, fill = avg_percent, label = Label)) +
  geom_treemap(color = "white", size = 2) +
  geom_treemap_text(
    color = "white", 
    place = "centre", 
    size = 12, 
    fontface = "bold", 
    grow = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#EF5350", high = "#B71C1C",
    labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    name = "Avg. % Thefts (Kia/Hyundai)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 15 U.S. Cities for Kia/Hyundai Thefts",
    subtitle = "Based on Motherboard VICE data (avg. across months)",
    caption = "Source: Motherboard VICE Investigation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, color = "gray40", hjust = 0.5)
  )
```

```{r}
# Filter geographic car theft map data with significant changes
geo_hotspots <- car_theft_map %>%
  filter(!is.na(percentChange2019to2022), # filter out rows with missing data
         !is.na(latitude), # keep only rows with coords
         !is.na(longitude),
         percentChange2019to2022 > 0) %>% # only positive changes
  arrange(desc(percentChange2019to2022)) %>% # order by descending
  mutate(
    Change_Category = cut(percentChange2019to2022, # add a new column to bucket categories
                          breaks = quantile(percentChange2019to2022,
                                            probs = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)),
                          labels = c("0-50%", "50-100%", "100-200%", ">200%"))
  )
```

```{r}
scatter_map <- ggplot(geo_hotspots, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = percentChange2019to2022, color = Change_Category),
             alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 15), labels = scales::percent_format(scale = 1),
                       name = "Theft Increase\n(2019-2022)") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#FFA726", "#FF7043", "#E53935", "#B71C1C"),
                    name = "Change Category") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "gray40"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Hotspots of Vehicle Theft Increases Across America",
    subtitle = "City-level percent change in vehicle thefts (2019-2022)",
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude"
  )
scatter_map

```
